notes: Several meaningful violations found: (1) ARCHITECTURAL RULE 1 BROKEN - The router directly calls `this.taskSvc.getTask(taskId)` inside the comment POST handler to fetch task data for notification purposes, then publishes `comment.added` with the task snapshot. This is a workaround that violates the no-direct-service-to-service rule in spirit, but the router itself is also performing cross-service data assembly which is not its role. (2) DOUBLE EVENT PUBLISH for comment.added - CommentService.addComment() publishes `comment.added` internally, AND the router also publishes `comment.added` with the enriched payload. This means NotificationService receives two events per comment: once with raw comment data (no task), once with enriched data. The notification logic only works on the enriched payload, but the first fire silently does nothing — a subtle but real bug. (3) RULE 3 VIOLATED - The router is doing business logic (cross-service data joining for comment+task) rather than pure HTTP delegation. (4) Task spec says `assigneeId` but implementation uses `assignee` inconsistently in types vs spec; `memberIds` in spec becomes `members` — minor but a spec mismatch. (5) Status transition allows same-status reassignment (newIdx === curIdx passes), which may or may not be intended but fires a spurious status_changed event. (6) `setStatus` allows backward transitions to be blocked but same-status re-sets pass and emit events. (7) No email uniqueness validation for users. (8) DELETE /projects/:id/members sends body with userId — some HTTP clients drop body on DELETE, fragile design. (9) `task.status_changed` event name in notification-service uses underscore but is consistent with TaskService publish call — OK. (10) NotificationService comment.added handler references `comment.task` and `comment.comment` assuming enriched payload, but raw payload from CommentService is just the Comment object — the dual-publish bug means the handler must be resilient to both shapes and is not. Overall the code is clean and readable but has a critical double-publish bug and meaningful architectural constraint violations.
